option_relations.rationale: Viral exanthem is a general term for a rash caused by a viral infection. While the patient has a rash, the specific findings in the vignette (epidermal necrosis, acantholysis, multinucleated keratinocytes) are not typical for a generic viral exanthem and do not directly relate to Stevens-Johnson Syndrome.
This option describes a specific type of COVID-19-associated skin eruption. While the vignette mentions negative SARS-CoV-2 tests on skin, the option itself is not Stevens-Johnson Syndrome.

This option describes a COVID-19-related varicella-like exanthem. The vignette describes pseudovesicular papules, but the histological findings are not consistent with varicella, and the option is not Stevens-Johnson Syndrome.
This option is a broad category. While the patient has cutaneous manifestations, this option does not specify Stevens-Johnson Syndrome.
